subject: lincomb in a model with vector response

messages.author: bdac8f1b7023ffbe
messages.subject: lincomb in a model with vector response
parts:
I am struggling with how to specify estimation of specific linear combinations of interest in a model with Gaussian vector response (either via lincomb or via A matrix).

Say , I have 4 responses and specify a model like:
v5<-inla(Y~-1+int.1+int.2.1+int.3.2+int.4.3+        
+f(mesic.1,model="rw1")+
f(mesic.2.1,model="rw1")+
f(mesic.3.2,model="rw1")+
f(mesic.4.3,model="rw1"),
         family=c("gaussian","gaussian","gaussian","gaussian"),  
data=list(Y=Y,
int.1=prac$int.1,int.2.1=prac$int.2.1,int.3.2=prac$int.3.2,int.4.3=prac$int.4.3,                  mesic.1=prac$mesic.1,mesic.2.1=prac$mesic.2.1,mesic.3.2=prac$mesic.3.2,
mesic.4.3=prac$mesic.4.3),
         control.compute=list(dic=T,waic=T),
         control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE)

The predictors are specified in an incremental way (both intercepts and smooth parts):
prac<-data.frame(vyska=rep(c(1,2,3,4),rep(nrow(smaz),4)),
                 o3.1=c(smaz$o3.1,rep(NA,3*n)),
                 o3.2=c(rep(NA,n),smaz$o3.2,rep(NA,2*n)),
                 o3.3=c(rep(NA,2*n),smaz$o3.3,rep(NA,n)),
                 o3.4=c(rep(NA,3*n),smaz$o3.4),
                 #    
                 int.1=rep(1,4*n),
                 int.2.1=c(rep(NA,n),rep(1,3*n)),
                 int.3.2=c(rep(NA,2*n),rep(1,2*n)),
                 int.4.3=c(rep(NA,3*n),rep(1,n)),
                 #
                 mesic.1=rep(smaz$mesic,4),
                 mesic.2.1=c(rep(NA,n),rep(smaz$mesic,3)),
                 mesic.3.2=c(rep(NA,2*n),rep(smaz$mesic,2)),
                mesic.4.3=c(rep(NA,3*n),smaz$mesic)      
              )
First question is whether the incremental way of specifying the model is OK (does not create some obvious computational problem)?

Now I would like to compute things like:
l1<-inla.make.lincombs(int.1 =  prac[1:n, "int.1"],mesic.1 =  prac[1:n, "mesic.1"]) 
i.e. sums involving both intercepts (one as here or more, later) and smooth terms (one as here or more, later). 
The specification of l1 is inspired by the previous post "Interactions and linear combinations in a joint likelihood model", but there were only regression terms, no smooth part ... 

While the model without  "lincom=l1," runs quite quickly and seems to give reasonable answers (quite in line with what I get by other approches), adding even the simple combination l1 slows it down tremendeously. Moreover, the estimated l1's (e.g. in the section "Linear combinations (derived):" are completely different from what I would expect. Probably, my specification of the linear combination is wrong. How to do it correctly? 

Or, is it better to get the answer via A matrix and stack? How? 

All the Best
 Marek
